verdict.rationale: Ledgy lets a company create API service accounts whose credentials are scoped per integration. These use short-lived OAuth 2.0 client_credentials tokens and can be revoked immediately, so an authorized third-party integration can reach cap table data without admin login credentials. The evidence does not show that a service account can be limited to a specific slice of equity data, and it describes no delegated third-party authorization flow. The in-app permission segmentation applies to team members and is a separate feature. Missing for 10: documented data-level permission scopes for service accounts (e.g. read-only or per-dataset), a delegated authorization flow for third parties such as law firms or wealth managers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, third parties my company authorizes — law firms, HRIS vendors, wealth managers — can access scoped slices of equity data on our behalf without full admin credentials

citations.quote: the credentials are scoped per integration, the tokens are short-lived, and revocation takes effect immediately
Create one in the Ledgy app under Company Settings → General → API service accounts
Exchange the credentials for an access token using the OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant
Revoke deletes the service account and invalidates its outstanding access tokens right away.
